card.summary: In pandas 3.1.0, `DataFrame.swapaxes` is gone, and the `method`, `limit`, `fill_axis` and `broadcast_axis` keywords of `DataFrame.align` are removed. Several keywords are deprecated: `copy` on `DataFrame.merge`, `DataFrame.align` and `DataFrame.transpose`; `dropna`, `sort` and `future_stack` on `DataFrame.stack`; `verify_integrity` on `DataFrame.set_index` (all since 3.0); and `inplace` on `DataFrame.set_index` and `DataFrame.reset_index`, plus `lsuffix`/`rsuffix` on `DataFrame.join` (since 3.1.0).

traps.trap: Calling `DataFrame.swapaxes` to swap rows and columns.
traps.instead: Use `DataFrame.transpose`.
traps.evidence: ``swapaxes`` is deprecated and will be removed. Please use ``transpose`` instead.

traps.trap: Passing `method`, `limit`, `fill_axis` or `broadcast_axis` to `DataFrame.align` to fill while aligning.
traps.instead: Call `DataFrame.align` with only `join`, `axis`, `level` and `fill_value`. Do any forward or backward filling as a separate step on the aligned result.
traps.evidence: level: 'Level | None' = None, copy: 'bool | lib.NoDefault' = <no_default>, fill_value: 'Hashable | None' = None)

traps.trap: Passing `lsuffix=` and `rsuffix=` to `DataFrame.join` for overlapping column names.
traps.instead: Pass one tuple, for example `suffixes=("_l", "_r")`, to `DataFrame.join`.
traps.evidence: Use ``suffixes`` instead.

traps.trap: Using `inplace=True` with `DataFrame.set_index` or `DataFrame.reset_index`.
traps.instead: Assign the returned frame: `df = df.set_index("key")` or `df = df.reset_index()`.
traps.evidence: This keyword is deprecated and will be removed in pandas 4.0. See the `whatsnew note on PDEP-8

traps.trap: Passing `verify_integrity=True` to `DataFrame.set_index` to reject duplicate keys.
traps.instead: Call `DataFrame.set_index` without it. Then check uniqueness on the result's index yourself, as the deprecation note says.
traps.evidence: The ``verify_integrity`` keyword is deprecated and will be removed in a future version. Check ``result.index.is_unique`` directly instead.

traps.trap: Passing `dropna=`, `sort=` or `future_stack=` to `DataFrame.stack`.
traps.instead: Call `DataFrame.stack` with only `level`. The new stack implementation is already the default.
traps.evidence: This parameter is deprecated and will be removed in a future version of pandas.

traps.trap: Passing `copy=False` or `copy=True` to `DataFrame.merge`, `DataFrame.align` or `DataFrame.transpose`.
traps.instead: Drop the keyword. Copy-on-Write always returns a new object with a lazy copy.
traps.evidence: This keyword is ignored and will be removed in pandas 4.0. Since pandas 3.0, this method always returns a new object using a lazy copy mechanism

example.explains: This script uses the 3.1.0 forms with every warning raised as an error: `DataFrame.merge` and `DataFrame.join` with `suffixes`, `DataFrame.set_index` with reassignment, `DataFrame.transpose` in place of the removed swapaxes, `DataFrame.align` with `fill_value` only, and `DataFrame.stack` without its deprecated keywords.
example.code:
import warnings
warnings.simplefilter("error")
import pandas as pd

left = pd.DataFrame({"key": ["a", "b", "c"], "val": [1, 2, 3]})
right = pd.DataFrame({"key": ["a", "b", "d"], "val": [10, 20, 40]})

# merge: no copy keyword
merged = left.merge(right, on="key", how="inner", suffixes=("_l", "_r"))
assert list(merged.columns) == ["key", "val_l", "val_r"]
assert list(merged["val_r"]) == [10, 20]

# set_index: reassign instead of the inplace keyword
l_idx = left.set_index("key")
r_idx = right.set_index("key")
assert list(l_idx.index) == ["a", "b", "c"]

# join: one suffixes tuple instead of lsuffix/rsuffix
joined = l_idx.join(r_idx, how="inner", suffixes=("_l", "_r"))
assert list(joined.columns) == ["val_l", "val_r"]
assert list(joined["val_r"]) == [10, 20]

# transpose replaces the removed swapaxes
t = joined.transpose()
assert list(t.columns) == ["a", "b"]
assert list(t.index) == ["val_l", "val_r"]

# align: only join and fill_value, no method/limit/fill_axis
a, b = l_idx.align(r_idx, join="outer", fill_value=0)
assert list(a.index) == ["a", "b", "c", "d"]
assert list(a["val"]) == [1, 2, 3, 0]
assert list(b["val"]) == [10, 20, 0, 40]

# stack: no dropna/sort/future_stack keywords
stacked = joined.stack()
assert len(stacked) == 4
assert stacked[("a", "val_r")] == 10
assert stacked[("b", "val_l")] == 2
print("ok")

failures: reshape-frame.md block 1: .simplefilter is not in pandas 3.1.0
